How to Use Kimi K3: Access, API Setup, and Pricing (2026)

Kimi K3 is Moonshot AI's flagship model: 2.8 trillion total parameters (104 billion active per token), a 1,048,576 token context window, and native image and video understanding. It launched the week of July 14, 2026, and Moonshot has since released the full weights under its own Kimi K3 License. This guide covers the practical part: how to get access, what it costs, and how the run-it-yourself option really works. For the full spec rundown, see our What Is Kimi K3 explainer.
Checked September 26, 2026 against Moonshot's own docs. Update box added October 24, 2026.

October 2026 update: Kimi K3.1 Pro is out, and it costs less than K3. Moonshot now lists kimi-k3.1-pro as its flagship and recommends it as the starting model in its quickstart. It is a post-trained version of K3 with the same 1M-token context, priced at $2.00 per million input tokens, $0.20 cached and $10.00 output, against $3.00 / $0.30 / $15.00 for K3. A faster variant, kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed, runs about 2-3x faster at $4.00 / $20.00. K3.1 Pro weights are promised by November 4, 2026. Everything below still works for K3, which Moonshot keeps on the API as its previous-generation model; to switch, change the model string to kimi-k3.1-pro. Same $1 minimum top-up, same base URL. Sources: Kimi API quickstart, K3.1 Pro guide, pricing, read October 24, 2026.

There are two ways to use it: the consumer chat app at kimi.com or the developer API. The open weights on Hugging Face are covered further down, in the section on running it locally. This guide walks through both access paths, with a working code snippet for the API path and the current published pricing.
Quick Answer
Chat app: go to kimi.com and start a conversation. Moonshot's K3 launch post lists the Kimi app (web, iOS, Android, HarmonyOS) as one of the ways to use K3.

API: sign up at platform.kimi.ai, top up at least $1 (Moonshot unlocks K3 after a successful top-up), generate a key, and call https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 with an OpenAI-compatible request. Model ID: kimi-k3.

Pricing (checked September 26, 2026, Moonshot's official rate card): $3.00 per million input tokens, $0.30 per million cached input tokens, $15.00 per million output tokens. Cache writes cost $3.00 per million (5 minute TTL) or $6.00 per million (1 hour TTL).
Open-weight: yes. Moonshot publishes the full weights at huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3 under the Kimi K3 License, a custom license with conditions for large commercial users (details below).

How to Access Kimi K3 (Two Paths)
1. The Consumer App: kimi.com

The fastest way to try K3 with no setup. Moonshot's launch post points people to the Kimi app and the website to use K3, so opening kimi.com and starting a chat is the right first step if you just want to test what K3 can do before wiring up an integration. Moonshot also lists the Kimi Work desktop app and the Kimi Code terminal tool as K3 entry points.
2. The Developer API: platform.kimi.ai
For anything programmatic, coding agents, internal tools, batch jobs, you'll want the API. Here's the setup path:
Create an account at platform.kimi.ai.
Top up at least $1. Moonshot's K3 quickstart says K3 "is unlocked after a successful top-up (minimum $1)", and your cumulative top-up sets your rate-limit tier.
Open the API Keys section of the console and generate a new key, then set it as an environment variable (MOONSHOT_API_KEY is the name Moonshot's own quickstart docs use).
Point your client at the base URL: https://api.moonshot.ai/v1.

One thing worth flagging if you've read older coverage of Kimi's API: some older guides point to api.moonshot.cn/v1. Moonshot's current quickstart docs at platform.kimi.ai list the base URL as https://api.moonshot.ai/v1. Use that value and confirm it in Moonshot's docs before you ship.

The API is OpenAI-format compatible (Moonshot also documents an Anthropic Messages compatible format), so if you already have code calling an OpenAI-style chat completions endpoint, switching over is mostly a matter of changing the base URL, key, and model string.

Kimi K3 Pricing: What It Actually Costs
Moonshot's pricing page for the K3 series lists these rates for kimi-k3:
Source: platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat-k3, checked September 26, 2026. Prices exclude taxes.

The cache is the detail worth planning around. Moonshot's docs say the API automatically caches repeated request prefixes, and input that hits the cache is billed at the $0.30 cached rate, a tenth of the $3.00 input rate, with each hit refreshing the cache entry at no extra write charge. Structure your prompts so the stable, reusable parts come first and the part that changes per request comes last, which is standard practice for prompt caching in general and applies here too.

Separately, Moonshot's pricing docs note that file-related APIs (file content extraction and file storage) are temporarily free. Text you extract and then pass to the model is still billed as input. "Temporarily" is Moonshot's word, so don't build a cost model that assumes it stays that way.

For comparison, Moonshot's same rate card lists Kimi K3.1 Pro at $2.00 input, $0.20 cached input and $10.00 output per million tokens (cache writes $2.00 for 5 minutes, $4.00 for 1 hour), so the newer model is a third cheaper on every line (checked October 24, 2026).
Pricing can change without much notice. Check Moonshot's live pricing page before you commit budget to it.
What Kimi K3 Is Good For (and What It Isn't)

Moonshot's K3 quickstart describes it as "designed for frontier intelligence scenarios including long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning," and its API overview calls it "well suited for programming agent scenarios such as Claude Code." Combined with the 1 million token context window and native image and video understanding, that points to a few concrete use cases:
Long-running coding agents. The context window is large enough to hold a substantial codebase or a long multi-step task history without truncation.
Document-heavy knowledge work. Feed it long reports, transcripts, or research bundles and ask it to reason across all of it at once.
Multimodal input tasks. Moonshot's vision guide lists kimi-k3 among the models that understand both images and video, so you can pass visual context alongside text without a separate pipeline.
What to watch for:

Open weights, custom license. The weights are public, but the Kimi K3 License is not MIT or Apache. If you run a Model as a Service business and you and your affiliates earn more than $20 million over any 12 months, you need a separate agreement with Moonshot before commercial use. Products with more than 100 million monthly active users or more than $20 million in monthly revenue must display "Kimi K3" in the UI. Internal use is exempt from both conditions. Read the license text yourself before you ship.

Benchmarks are vendor-reported. Moonshot's model card publishes benchmark tables, run at reasoning effort max, many in its own Kimi Code harness, plus some scores it cites from Artificial Analysis. Treat them as Moonshot's numbers until independent evaluators publish their own.

Always in reasoning mode. Moonshot's docs say K3 "always has thinking mode enabled" and expose a reasoning_effort request field (low, high, or max, default max) rather than an on/off switch. If you need the fastest, cheapest response for a simple task, set reasoning_effort to low rather than expecting a separate non-reasoning model.

Pass the full assistant message back. For multi-turn chats and tool calls, Moonshot says to send the complete assistant message returned by the API back in messages, including reasoning_content and tool_calls, not just content.
Running Kimi K3 Locally
Moonshot's own model card recommends three inference engines for the native weights: vLLM, SGLang, and TokenSpeed. At 2.8 trillion parameters, serving the full weights is a multi-GPU server job.

The smaller option comes from Unsloth, not Moonshot. Unsloth's Kimi K3 run-locally guide and its Kimi-K3-GGUF repository (files uploaded July 29 to August 7, 2026, per the repo history) offer quantized GGUF versions of Moonshot's weights, still under the Kimi K3 License. Here's exactly what the guide covers:

Quant sizes. Files range from a 594 GB dynamic 1-bit (UD-IQ1_S, which Unsloth recommends) through 2-bit versions up to about 1.51 TB (4-bit) and 1.56 TB (8-bit, which Unsloth calls lossless against Moonshot's MXFP4 weights).

Hardware. Unsloth's rule of thumb is that RAM plus VRAM should roughly equal the quant size, and the 1-bit walkthrough "will require at least 610GB RAM." Below that it still runs, but much slower because it offloads to disk.
Tools. Step-by-step instructions for Unsloth Studio (Unsloth's desktop app) and llama.cpp, using Unsloth's llama.cpp fork that adds vision support.
Settings. temperature 1.0 with top_p 0.95 by default, or top_p 1.0 for agentic tasks, and reasoning_effort low, high, or max.

Unsloth reports that its 1-bit quant keeps about 78.9% top-1 agreement with the full model. That is Unsloth's measurement, not Moonshot's. For most teams, the API at $3 and $15 per million tokens will cost far less than hardware with 600 GB or more of memory.

Tips for Getting the Most Out of Kimi K3

Tune reasoning_effort to the task. Moonshot's docs expose this as a top-level request field with three settings. Save max for genuinely hard, multi-step problems and drop to low for straightforward lookups or formatting tasks, since reasoning effort affects both latency and output token count (which is what you're billed for).

Structure prompts for cache hits. Put stable content, system instructions, reference documents, tool definitions, ahead of the part of the prompt that changes each call. That's what makes the $0.30 cached input rate apply instead of the $3.00 input rate.
Don't hardcode the base URL from an old tutorial. Pull the current value from Moonshot's docs rather than copying it from a guide, including this one, without checking the date.
Keep the model string configurable. Moonshot's current docs, pricing page, and model card all use kimi-k3, but keep it in config so a future model swap is a one-line change.
FAQ

How do I use Kimi K3? Through the consumer app at kimi.com for chat, or through Moonshot's API at api.moonshot.ai/v1 for programmatic access. The API uses an OpenAI-compatible request format with the model ID kimi-k3. You can also download the open weights from Hugging Face and run them on your own hardware.

Is Kimi K3 free? Not on the API. Moonshot charges $3.00 per million input tokens, $0.30 per million cached input tokens, and $15.00 per million output tokens, checked September 26, 2026, and K3 unlocks after a minimum $1 top-up. File extraction and storage APIs are temporarily free. The weights themselves are free to download under the Kimi K3 License.

What is the Kimi K3 API base URL? https://api.moonshot.ai/v1, per Moonshot's current quickstart documentation. Some older guides show api.moonshot.cn/v1, so confirm the live value in Moonshot's docs before you build against it.

Is Kimi K3 open-weight? Yes. Moonshot released the full Kimi K3 weights on Hugging Face at moonshotai/Kimi-K3, and its docs call it open-source. The license is the custom Kimi K3 License, not MIT or Apache: large Model as a Service businesses need a separate agreement, and very large products must display "Kimi K3" in their UI.

How do I run Kimi K3 locally? Moonshot recommends vLLM, SGLang, or TokenSpeed for the full weights, a multi-GPU server job at 2.8 trillion parameters. For smaller setups, Unsloth publishes GGUF quants with a llama.cpp and Unsloth Studio guide. Its smallest recommended file is 594 GB, and Unsloth says RAM plus VRAM should roughly match the file size.

Does Kimi K3 support images and video? Yes. Moonshot's vision guide lists kimi-k3 among the models that can understand both images and video content, and its model card describes K3 as natively multimodal rather than routing images through a separate vision model.

Should I use Kimi K3 or Kimi K3.1 Pro? For new projects, K3.1 Pro. Moonshot calls it its most capable model and recommends it in the quickstart, and it is cheaper: $2.00 input and $10.00 output per million tokens versus $3.00 and $15.00 for K3 (October 24, 2026). The API call is the same; only the model ID changes to kimi-k3.1-pro. Stay on kimi-k3 if you have already tested and tuned prompts against it, or if you need K3's open weights today, since K3.1 Pro weights are only promised by November 4, 2026.

Are older Kimi models being retired? The K2 series is. Moonshot's pricing page says K2 models stop being available to newly registered users on October 31, 2026, and all K2 models are planned to retire by the end of December 2026. Existing users are not affected until then. K3 is still listed as an available model.
How does Kimi K3 compare to Claude Fable 5? On specs, availability, and price. Moonshot's model card includes Fable 5 in its own benchmark tables, but those are vendor-run numbers.
